verified.exploit_entry_point: library API expect(value).toMatchFileSnapshot(path) through the assertions wrapper; the snapshot store routes through SnapshotClient.loadSnapshots/saveSnapshots, SnapshotManager.finishFile/cleanup and NodeSnapshotEnvironment.saveSnapshotFile/removeSnapshotFile, all reachable by the project's own tests
routes: T1: absolute path outside the project, create and overwrite branches, and the parent directories created before the write
T2: the compare branch reads the outside file and repeats its content in the mismatch error
T3: relative traversal and a link inside the project whose target is outside it
T5: store write outside an absolute configured directory, through the client, the manager and the environment itself
T6: store removal outside an absolute configured directory, direct and through a link inside it
verified.project_tests_run: bun test --no-coverage tests/unit/snapshot-matchers.test.ts tests/unit/snapshot-client.test.ts tests/unit/snapshot-improvements.test.ts: 65 pass on the pinned tree (run in the image build); every security/functional check patch was exercised against the pinned tree before the gate

traps.shape: a file-snapshot assertion path that resolves outside the project is used unmodified: the create branch makes its parent directories and writes the file there, and the overwrite branch rewrites it there; no confinement decision exists
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-322X-V876-G883) at the pinned commit

traps.shape: the compare branch reads the caller-supplied path and folds its content into the mismatch error, so a guard placed only around the write branches still lets content outside the project be read
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the advisory is arbitrary file write, not read; repeating the stored value in a mismatch error is treated as harmless, so guarding the write paths is argued to be sufficient
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the published fix did not have to touch this branch separately because it guarded the whole function

traps.shape: a path that is lexically inside the project but whose existing ancestor is a link to a directory outside it; a resolve-and-prefix comparison passes it and the write or read follows the link
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the repository's own confinement idiom resolves absolute paths and compares strings (src/coverage/filter.ts:84-90), and a lexical prefix check is exactly the shape the published fix describes
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the pinned function has no check and the published lexical check leaves this form open

traps.shape: the snapshot store writes the caller-supplied filepath through its environment with no confinement to the directory the environment was given; a client, a manager and the environment itself all reach the write
traps.reason_to_dismiss: an absolute snapshot directory is a supported, tested configuration and the path comes from the runner's test-file list rather than from the snapshot assertion argument; the store is a separate internal implementation not part of the package's public export
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the write path is still unconfined in current upstream, where a later fix only rejects '..' and final-component links

traps.shape: the snapshot store unlinks the caller-supplied filepath with no confinement to the directory the environment was given
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the advisory is arbitrary file write, not deletion, and cleanup only removes paths the runner itself resolved, so the removal path is argued to be out of scope
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; removeSnapshotFile is still unconfined in current upstream
